newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey, Hungary to sign free trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: Turkey, Hungary to sign free trade agreement.

text.p: Turkey and Hungary will sign a free trade agreement this week that could more than double trade between the two countries, a Turkish official said on Monday.
"A Turkish delegation headed by State Minister Ayfer Yilmaz will go to Hungary tomorrow," said Reyhan Atmaca, general manager of the EU Section at the Foreign Trade Undersecretariat.
"The agreement is part of our fulfillment for the third countries after the customs union. We hope to reap benefits from the customs deal with the EU," she told Reuters.

A lucrative customs deal between Turkey and the European Union went into effect at the start of 1996, which abolished customs duties for many industrial products and envisaged a common policy towards trade with third countries.
Atmaca said the free trade deal with Hungary was aimed at boosting bilateral trade to $500 million a year from $200 million now.

She said the agreement would include a a newly-introduced quota of 12,000 tonnes for Turkish citrus products to Hungary and also benefits that Turkey will get from Hungary's recent trade agreement with the EU.

Free trade agreements, which include trade of industrial goods, some agricultural products and processed fooditems, bring Turkey in line with the EU terms in trade with third countries. It has so far signed such agreements with several countries.

Officials said an agreement with Israel, signed in March last year, was approved by the Israeli parliament, but it was being held up by the Islamist wing of the Turkish cabinet who have opposed developing ties with Israel.

Atmaca said the Israeli deal would boost the trade volume to $1 billion annually from $400 million now and this would also pave the way for more trade with the United States and the Palestinian self-rule territories.
Turkey will also sign free trade agreements with Lithuania, Czech Republic, Slovenia and Poland soon, she said.
